name: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
problem: BERT must run both sentences through the network jointly, making similarity search over a corpus quadratically expensive.
mechanism: Siamese/triplet structure with a SHARED encoder and a pooling layer producing one fixed-size vector per sentence; similarity is then a cosine or dot product over precomputed vectors. This makes the encoder independent per sentence, so corpus vectors are computed once and indexable.
speedup_reported: Reduces the cost of finding the most similar pair in a 10,000-sentence collection from ~65 HOURS (about 50 million BERT inference computations) to about 5 SECONDS, while retaining BERT's accuracy. The 10,000-sentence corpus and the CPU-class baseline are both stated, which makes this the most concrete encoder-cost number in the embedding literature.
notes: Venue EMNLP 2019, confirmed via crossref (ACL, 'Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing'). The single most consequential paper for embedding SERVING: it is the reason embedding workloads are a vector-database problem rather than an inference problem. THE COST INVERSION THIS REPO CARES ABOUT: a text encoder at batch 1 is COMPUTE-BOUND, the inverse of a batch-1 text decoder which is memory-bound. One SBERT forward is a few GFLOPs and reads all weights, so batching is not optional - unlike decode, where batching is opportunistic. Everything about encoder serving (batch it, sort by length, keep weights resident) follows from that.
